claims.claim_text: The matrix separates cognitive and affective empathy, sympathy, and compassion, then profiles psychopath, sociopath, empath, altruist, and integrated ideal.
claims.evidence_quote: The four component columns (cognitive and affective empathy, sympathy, compassion) sit left of the double rule. The five to the right are whole-person profiles ... psychopath, sociopath, empath, altruist, and the integrated ideal.
claims.reasoning: Source names the same four components and five profiles in the same order.

claims.claim_text: Four components sit left of the double rule; five dark-to-light profiles sit right.
claims.evidence_quote: The four component columns ... sit left of the double rule. The five to the right are whole-person profiles, arranged darkest to lightest
claims.reasoning: Direct restatement of source layout and darkest-to-lightest ordering.

claims.claim_text: Rows fall in four blocks: present in both, psychopath only, sociopath only, neither.
claims.evidence_quote: four blocks separated by blank dividers: present in both, in the psychopath only, in the sociopath only, and in neither.
claims.reasoning: Exact parallel to the source's four block names.

claims.claim_text: Cognitive empathy means accurate modeling, boundary, and control; it survives in manipulators.
claims.evidence_quote: Can exist in manipulators / con artists: cognitive check only ... Controlled / instrumental rather than reactive / impulsive: cognitive check
claims.reasoning: Table gives cognitive checks on modeling, boundary, manipulators, and control as stated.

claims.claim_text: The psychopath column is essentially the cognitive-empathy column standing alone.
claims.evidence_quote: the psychopath is close to the cognitive-empathy column standing alone
claims.reasoning: Note 6 and Note 10 both state this; 'essentially' matches 'standing alone'.

claims.claim_text: Sympathy earns only partial on modeling: pity can badly misread people.
claims.evidence_quote: Sympathy gets "~" on modeling the other's mind because you can pity someone while badly misreading them.
claims.reasoning: Source explicitly gives sympathy a tilde for misreading while pitying.

claims.claim_text: Affective empathy means sharing emotion, with contagion, burnout, and vividness bias.
claims.evidence_quote: Actually sharing / mirroring the emotion ... Risk of emotional contagion and burnout: affective check ... Biased toward vivid, similar individuals: ... affective check
claims.reasoning: Table assigns affective checks to sharing, contagion/burnout, and vividness bias.

claims.claim_text: Affective empathy lacks boundary maintenance, unlike everything else in the table.
claims.evidence_quote: Boundary maintenance is the structural difference between affective empathy and everything else in the table
claims.reasoning: Note 5 states boundary is the structural difference for affective empathy.

claims.claim_text: Affective empathy earns only partial on caring: contagion can occur without concern.
claims.evidence_quote: Affective empathy gets "~" on "capacity to care": emotional contagion can happen involuntarily, without any real concern for the person
claims.reasoning: Note 2 states the tilde and the without-concern condition exactly.

claims.claim_text: The sociopath resembles affective empathy plus sympathy clamped to an in-group, unregulated.
claims.evidence_quote: the sociopath is close to the affective-empathy and sympathy columns clamped to a narrow in-group and stripped of regulation
claims.reasoning: Note 6 matches the affective/sympathy clamp and loss of regulation.

claims.claim_text: Compassion alone combines caring, motivation to help, wide scope, and sustainability.
claims.evidence_quote: Motivation to help or act: ... compassion check ... Concern reaches beyond a vivid / similar in-group: ... compassion check ... Sustainable and scalable as a moral guide: ... compassion check
claims.reasoning: Among the four components only compassion is checked on all listed rows.

claims.claim_text: Only compassion scores full marks on helping motivation and sustainable scalable guidance.
claims.evidence_quote: Motivation to help or act: affective partial, sympathy partial, compassion check ... Sustainable and scalable as a moral guide: cognitive partial, sympathy partial, compassion check
claims.reasoning: Only compassion carries a check on both rows among components.

claims.claim_text: The Bloom and Singer pro-compassion case is a position, not a consensus.
claims.evidence_quote: the Bloom/Singer argument ... which is a position, not a consensus
claims.reasoning: Note 4 states the position-not-consensus framing verbatim.

claims.claim_text: The psychopath keeps only cold instrumental control; the sociopath holds the affective cluster.
claims.evidence_quote: cold instrumental control is the psychopath's one distinguishing possession, while a whole cluster of affective and caring rows belongs to the sociopath and not the psychopath
claims.reasoning: Note 6 states both halves of the asymmetry.

claims.claim_text: Almost all psychopath traits recur degraded in sociopath; only control is psychopath-only.
claims.evidence_quote: almost everything the psychopath has, the sociopath also has in degraded form, so the psychopath's one distinguishing possession is cold instrumental control
claims.reasoning: Direct paraphrase preserving the quantifier 'almost' and the single distinguishing trait.

claims.claim_text: Emotion-sharing, caring, helping, guilt, and contagion rows belong to sociopath, not psychopath.
claims.evidence_quote: Block sociopath-only rows. Actually sharing / mirroring the emotion ... Capacity to genuinely care ... Motivation to help or act ... Produces guilt / remorse ... Risk of emotional contagion and burnout
claims.reasoning: These rows are listed in the sociopath-only block, absent for psychopath.

claims.claim_text: The empath maximizes affect unregulated, so it is not the moral ideal.
claims.evidence_quote: The empath is the affective column maxed out and unregulated ... it is not the moral ideal
claims.reasoning: Note 10 states maxed-out/unregulated and not-the-moral-ideal.

claims.claim_text: The empath lights up sharing, contagion, and bias but fails boundary, scope, and scalability.
claims.evidence_quote: it lights up emotion-sharing, contagion, and vividness bias while failing on boundary, scope, and scalability
claims.reasoning: Note 10 lists exactly these successes and failures.

claims.claim_text: The altruist embodies compassion and the Light Triad: Kantianism, Humanism, Faith in Humanity.
claims.evidence_quote: The altruist is the compassion column embodied, matching the research "Light Triad" (Kantianism, Humanism, and Faith in Humanity, from Kaufman et al., 2019)
claims.reasoning: Note 10 names the same three Light Triad components for the altruist.

claims.claim_text: The integrated ideal alone scores well across every block, opposing both dark profiles.
claims.evidence_quote: The integrated ideal is the only column that scores well across every block ... so it is the true opposite of both dark profiles at once
claims.reasoning: Note 10 states only-column and true-opposite claims.

claims.claim_text: Kantianism inverts the manipulators row; only Faith in Humanity adds a new dimension.
claims.evidence_quote: 'Treats people as ends, not means' (Kantianism) is essentially the inverse of the 'manipulators' row ... Only 'Believes people are fundamentally good' (Faith in Humanity) adds a genuinely new dimension
claims.reasoning: Note 11 states both the inversion and the sole new dimension.

claims.claim_text: The table limits its scope deliberately and treats dark columns as ideal types.
claims.evidence_quote: Etiology is deliberately left out as a row ... Treat these two columns as ideal types, not categories.
claims.reasoning: Notes 7 and 8 support the deliberate scope limit and ideal-types framing.

claims.claim_text: Etiology stays out: causal origin is not a response shape.
claims.evidence_quote: That is a claim about causes, not about the shape of the response, so it does not belong in a feature table.
claims.reasoning: Note 7 gives the same causes-versus-response rationale.

claims.claim_text: Psychopath and sociopath are not formal diagnoses; both fall under antisocial personality disorder.
claims.evidence_quote: "psychopath" and "sociopath" are not formal diagnoses. Both fall under Antisocial Personality Disorder
claims.reasoning: Note 8 states both the non-diagnosis and APD inclusion.

claims.claim_text: Terminology varies; empathic concern and pop-psych sympathy differ from table usage.
claims.evidence_quote: usage varies across the literature. Some authors use "empathic concern" roughly where this table uses "compassion," and pop-psych usage (e.g. Brené Brown) treats "sympathy" as inherently distancing.
claims.reasoning: Note 9 states both terminology variants and the neutral research sense used.
